subtopic: Tax Treatment of Cash Value, Death Benefits, and Loans
source_evidence: Your cash value may accumulate on a tax-deferred basis. This means you will only be subject to federal income tax when you withdraw money from your policy. The policy’s gains will be subject to ordinary federal income tax rates rather than lower capital gains rates. The death benefit paid to your beneficiaries is not subject to federal income tax. You may take loans from your policy without paying federal income taxes. However, if your policy terminates with a loan outstanding, you may owe federal income taxes on the loan.
answer: Variable life insurance has different federal income tax treatment for its cash value, death benefit, and policy loans. Cash value may grow tax-deferred, but withdrawals can trigger federal income tax on policy gains, which are taxed at ordinary income tax rates rather than lower capital gains rates. The death benefit paid to beneficiaries is not subject to federal income tax. Policy loans may be taken without paying federal income tax, but if the policy terminates while a loan is outstanding, federal income tax may be owed on that loan. Tax rules can be complicated, and state tax implications may also apply.
